hypothesis: Pure decomposition (Direction 4) still suffers from cross-domain noise: each sub-query traverses the full tree and may surface neighbours from the wrong L1 domain. If the decomposer LLM also tags each sub-query with its target L1 domain (chosen from the L1 description list already in the prompt), the traverser can be restricted to descend only that subtree. This removes domain-noise without removing intent-noise (which the leaf reranker handles), targeting the cross-domain co-call misses (e.g. 'validate this passport scan, then make a tracking id and hash it' splits cleanly across [reward, utils]).

papers.title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
papers.key_claim: A top-level decomposer prompt plans sub-tasks and dispatches each to a specialized handler from a library; the modular split outperforms monolithic chain-of-thought on multi-hop QA and symbolic reasoning.

baseline.direction4_expected: 0.85-0.88 (sets the comparison point for whether routing adds value)
baseline.miss_breakdown: Of the 19 partial-miss complex cases, ~3 are pure cross-domain co-calls (utility + reward, science + utility) where decomposition alone may still rank wrong-domain neighbours above the right tool

design.stage: pre-retrieval; tree unchanged. Builds on Direction 4's decompose_query.
design.prompt: Single LLM call. Output JSON: [{"sub_query": "...", "domain": "L1_id_or_any"}]. The L1 descriptions in the prompt now serve double duty: anchoring the split AND naming the routing options.
design.routing: For each pair: if domain != 'any', restrict traverser to subtree rooted at that L1 node (pass start_node param); else fall back to root traversal. Final fusion identical to Direction 4 (max score per tool across sub-queries).
design.fallback: If LLM picks a non-existent L1 id, log + degrade to root traversal for that sub-query. Never hard-fail.
files_to_touch: src/tool_index/retrieval/decompose.py - extend decompose_query to optionally return domain tags
src/tool_index/retrieval/traverser.py - extend retrieve(start_node=None) to descend from a given node id instead of root

measurement.metric: complex set-recall@10, complex full-cover, simple recall@10, plus per-case routing-correctness diagnostic (did the LLM pick a domain that contains at least one gold tool?)
ablation: Direction 5 with 'any' fallback always allowed (ablate the fallback)
measurement.success_threshold: complex set-recall@10 >= 0.90 AND simple recall@10 >= 0.97 AND >= +0.02 over Direction 4

risks: LLM picks the wrong L1 -> tool unreachable for that sub-query. Domain-routing precision must hit ~90% to break even vs Direction 4.
Adds prompt-format strictness (JSON schema with domain enum); model failures more visible. Use the existing markdown-fence-stripping helper.
Restricted traversal at L1 may miss tools that genuinely belong in two domains (rare in current catalog but possible at 10k scale).
decision_rule: Promote if complex set-recall@10 >= 0.90 AND >= +0.02 over Direction 4 AND simple recall@10 unchanged. If routing buys < 0.02 over D4, archive in favour of D4 (simpler).
